_comment: AER-679 moving-position pass threshold, narrowed by AER-1082, SVS provenance corrected by AER-1086, map bound corrected AER-2241. svs.frame_gap_ms.p95 stays gated at 50 ms == PROBE_GAP_WARN_MS (map/perf.py). The bar's old justification cited a DEMO-era figure (bench demo pattern swept ALT continuously with LAT/LONG pinned -- the exact regime AER-677 retired) and should never have sourced a live gate. AER-1086 re-measured on healthy current dev with the moving-position harness itself (--target svs, 130 kt/280 deg/20 Hz, 41 s, real GL via a shared X display -- offscreen QPA can't create a QOpenGLWidget context at all): p50 33.0 / p95 34.0 / p99 34.9 / max 35.6 ms, comfortably under 50 ms with collector hit rates >99% (frame_total_ms stayed ~4.6-5.0 ms, so the render itself is cheap, not starved). This also kills the suspected 'floored at the 20 Hz drive period' mechanism: SVS repaints on its own free-running 30 fps QTimer (ai/__init__.py set_frame_rate, default), not on position change, so the ~33 ms gap tracks that timer's nominal 33.3 ms period, not the 50 ms drive period. 50 ms therefore keeps clean margin (~16 ms) above the real healthy baseline. map.frame_gap_ms.p95 is NOT gated: AER-692 showed it is dominated by pose-quantization arithmetic (10 NM half-range, 130 kt -> ~266 ms to cross the half-pixel the pose gate requires, then a 10 Hz frame-clock boundary on top), so ~300 ms is the CORRECT designed answer for that scenario and a 50 ms bound on it is always-red regardless of code health. AER-2241: the map is gated on map.probe.over_count, NOT probe.p95_ms/max_ms -- GuiProbe's p50/p95/max are computed over a RING_SIZE=256 trailing ring (map/perf.py), which at the ~10 ms tick period saturates at ~2.6 s regardless of run length, so on this scenario's 41 s duration those percentiles see only the last ~6% of the run and a GIL stall anywhere in the first ~38 s leaves them untouched. over_count increments on every tick for the whole run and is the only field here that is evidence about the full window (maos-workspace PR #80 / AER-2238 section 5; oracle_gate.md reading rules 3-4: probe.p95_ms/probe.max_ms are non-citable on any scenario). See docs/moving_map_spec.md section 9.2.
